newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM to propose 98/99 budget by end-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM to propose 98/99 budget by end-Feb.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Friday he would propose a two-year budget for 1998-99 to parliament, which will give long-term signals to businessmen.
"The most important thing is to create a long-term future plan in order to provide correct signals to both local and foreign entrepreneurs," Shkele told a news conference.
He said that by the end of February the political framework of the next two-year budget should be ready.

Latvia, which renewed its independence from the Soviet Union in 1991, on Thursday received a BBB rating with a stable outlook to its long-term foreign currency debt from U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's (S&P).
S&P also assigned an A- rating to Latvia's long term local currency debt and an A-3 short term foreign currency and A-2 short term local currency rating.
"It is important to create a long-term philosophy...and also to prevent excessive political influences during the last year before parliamentary elections," Shkele added.
Latvia is expected to register gross domestic product (GDP) of around 2.5 percent for 1996 and year-on-year inflation of 13.1 percent, according to central bank forecasts.
The current parliament mandate expires at the end of 1998.
Shkele last December pushed through a balanced 1997 budget for the first time in Latvia's history and it also met its 40 million lat budget deficit target.
